Design the systems that guide satellites in orbit for new ambitious missions

We are seeking an experienced AOCS/GNC Engineer to design, develop, and validate attitude determination, orbit control, and autonomous navigation solutions for small satellite missions. In this role, you will develop guidance and control strategies across diverse and demanding mission profiles — from VLEO drag-dominated regimes to deep-space trajectories and asteroid proximity operations.

You will join our Advanced Missions global team, developing next-generation AOCS/GNC concepts while collaborating closely with GomSpace's established AOCS team in Aalborg — who built and flew the AOCS for the Juventas CubeSat on ESA's Hera mission and are currently developing full 6-DoF GNC for the Llevant (RAMSES) asteroid rendezvous mission.

**

Your Role**

As AOCS/GNC Engineer, you will own the attitude and orbit control design for advanced mission proposals — from requirements definition and algorithm design through high-fidelity simulation and hardware-in-the-loop validation.

Your key responsibilities include:

• Design and implement AOCS/GNC algorithms for attitude determination, control, and autonomous navigation across diverse mission profiles.

• Develop guidance and orbit-control strategies tailored to SSA, VLEO drag-dominated regimes, and deep-space trajectories.

• Model and simulate spacecraft dynamics, environmental disturbances, and sensor/actuator performance for mission-specific scenarios.

• Validate algorithms through high-fidelity simulations, Monte-Carlo analyses, and hardware-in-the-loop setups.

• Collaborate with systems, propulsion, and mission design teams to define control requirements and ensure end-to-end stability and performance.

**

What Success Looks Like**

In the initial phase, success means:

• Understanding GomSpace's AOCS product portfolio (GSW-600 reaction wheels, Auriga/Twinkle star trackers, STIM300 IMU, AOCS Flightcore software).

• Delivering your first AOCS sizing and mode analysis for a mission proposal and setting up a reusable MATLAB/Simulink simulation environment.

• Establishing working relationships with the Aalborg AOCS team and communicating AOCS trade-offs clearly to non-AOCS stakeholders.

Over time, you will be recognised for owning end-to-end AOCS/GNC design for advanced mission proposals, developing and maintaining GNC strategies across multiple mission regimes, and achieving successful Monte-Carlo validation campaigns that demonstrate algorithm robustness.

**

What You Bring**

You are an AOCS/GNC specialist with deep analytical rigour and a passion for solving complex spacecraft dynamics and control challenges across unconventional mission profiles.

You likely bring:

• An MSc or PhD in Aerospace Engineering, Astrodynamics, Control Systems, Applied Mathematics, or a related field. A PhD focused on GNC, spacecraft dynamics, or autonomous navigation is a strong plus.

• 3–5+ years of experience in AOCS/GNC algorithm design, simulation, and validation for spacecraft missions.

• Experience with attitude determination (gyro-stellar estimators, EKF/UKF), 3-axis control (sliding mode, PD/PID, LQR), and momentum management.

• Proficiency in MATLAB/Simulink for spacecraft dynamics modelling and Monte-Carlo analysis.

• Experience with C/C++ implementation of flight algorithms and familiarity with AOCS sensors and actuators (star trackers, IMUs, reaction wheels, magnetorquers, RCS thrusters).

• Exposure to ESA/ECSS project lifecycle and AOCS design reviews (PDR, CDR) is highly valued.

**

Who You Are**

You combine deep mathematical rigour with creative engineering intuition. You are energised by the challenge of designing control solutions for missions that push the boundaries of what nanosatellites can do.

You are known for:

• Analytical depth — AOCS/GNC demands mathematical precision, and you deliver it.

• Creative problem solving — developing novel control strategies for unconventional mission profiles.

• Collaborative communication — translating complex dynamics and control concepts into clear requirements for systems and propulsion teams.

• Self-driven initiative — comfortable with ambiguity in early-phase mission design.

• Execution discipline – ensuring commitments are met in demanding environments.

• Customer focus – ensuring focus on customer’s success.

• True leadership — taking ownership of your domain and driving technical excellence.

**

Why Join Us**

You will play a key role in shaping future space missions at their most decisive stage. This position offers the opportunity to work closely with leading institutional customers, influence mission architectures from the start, and contribute to programs with long-term strategic impact.

**

Join our mission**

You are welcome to send your application in English. Interviews will be conducted on a continuous basis. If you have any questions regarding the position do not hesitate to contact: Gaetano Livornese, Department Manager. E-mail: gali@gomspace.com

Workplace will be at our premises at Langagervej 6 in Aalborg, Denmark. Salary and start date will be individually negotiated.

We kindly draw your attention to the fact that we do not receive applications and resumes via e-mail or by personal appearance. This is to protect and show consideration for your personal information. Apply for the job by following the link below.

**

About GomSpace**

GomSpace is a globally leading designer, integrator and manufacturer of high-end nano and microsatellites for customers in the academic, government and commercial markets. Our positions of strength include systems integration, small satellite subsystems and advanced miniaturized radio technology. At the core of our mission are our core values: Be helpful, communicate openly and frequently, and show true leadership.

Our international team is devoted to understanding our customers’ requirements and delivering high quality. We are listed in Stockholm (GOMX), headquartered in Denmark and have subsidiaries in Sweden, Singapore, France, North America and Luxembourg. We have more than 200 employees servicing customers in more than 60 countries.

Learn more on www.gomspace.com

At GomSpace WE MAKE SPACE YOURS.

Join us in shaping the future of space exploration!

**

Application deadline:**

As soon as possible

jobs.description:
The Company

COWI is a leading international consultancy within engineering, architecture, energy, and the environment. In close collaboration with clients, COWI co-creates innovative and sustainable solutions that enhance quality of life for current and future generations. With a primary presence in Scandinavia, the United Kingdom, North America, and India, COWI employs approximately 7,500 professionals who bring expertise across a wide range of disciplines.

If you are curious to learn more, we invite you to explore some of COWI’s featured projects at www.cowi.com or view their global portfolio at: Projects around the world (cowi.com)

On behalf of COWI, Best Talent is now seeking an Associate Project Director.

The organisation & the Team

COWI’s Building & Industry Executing Unit in Denmark, consists of approximately 1050 professionals and specialists across building related disciplines.

Within this framework, you will be part of a dedicated Multidisciplinary Project Management team in Lyngby, consisting of approximately 38 committed colleagues. This structure ensures a strong, supportive, and highly professional environment focused on excellence in project delivery.

As part of this strong professional community, you will work alongside dedicated, talented, and ambitious colleagues who are strongly committed to excellence in project leadership and management. Moreover, you will have the opportunity to realize your full potential within an inclusive and supportive professional environment.

Associate Project Director

Exiting Multidisciplinary Building Projects – From Design to Execution

• Strong focus on clients and project delivery

• Thrive in a collaborative and supportive culture

• Shape your own professional development

• Contribute to a more sustainable and livable world

The Challenge

As Associated Project Director for construction projects in Denmark, you will be responsible for the comprehensive management of building projects—from initial planning through to execution. Your role will encompass quality assurance, budget control, contractual and financial oversight, as well as the coordination of timelines and resources.

You will also act as the key liaison with clients and collaborate closely with stakeholders such as public authorities, contractors, and design partners.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Leading new construction and renovation projects from concept to completion

• Participating in large-scale projects as part of a broader project management team

• Managing complex stakeholder environments, clients, authorities, contractors, and design partners

• Maintain close collaboration with clients to ensure their needs and expectations are consistently met

• Overseeing project scope, schedule, risks, and cost management

• Ensuring high standards of quality, safety, and sustainability across all project stages

• Driving cross-disciplinary collaboration across COWI’s teams and geographies

• Contributing to the professional development of project team members

Why join COWI?

At COWI, your work contributes to shaping a sustainable and liveable world. By combining deep knowledge, curiosity, and courage, COWI develops solutions that address today’s challenges and enable a better tomorrow. COWI has committed to phasing out fossil-based projects and aspires for 100% of its revenue to stem from sustainability-focused initiatives.

COWI values diversity, continuous development, and a sense of belonging. They foster a supportive and enjoyable workplace, knowing that a healthy work-life balance enhances performance both professionally and personally. You will report to the Vice President of the group and be offered a competitive compensation package, aligned with your experience and qualifications.

Your profile & Talent:

You are an experienced Multidisciplinary Project Manager who thrives in collaboration with colleagues, partners, and clients. You foster strong relationships through integrity, accountability, and a proactive mindset. Your background has equipped you to confidently lead medium- to large-scale design projects.

Qualifications and key competencies:

• A relevant academic background in civil engineering, architecture, or a related discipline

• Professional experience in Denmark, with in-depth knowledge of all phases of the Danish building project lifecycle

• Strong leadership and communication skills, with the ability to manage complex project environments

• A proactive and structured approach to work, with keen attention to detail

• A self-motivated and inspiring personality that promotes teamwork and positive dynamics

• Proficiency in Danish and English, both spoken and written

Diversity and inclusion:

Diversity is a core value at COWI, and inclusion is a strategic priority. The company is committed to fostering a respectful, equitable, and inclusive workplace where all employees feel a sense of belonging and have equal opportunities for growth. Leaders at COWI are expected to model inclusive behaviour and embrace diverse perspectives as a strength in team formation and decision-making processes. These commitments are not only embedded in COWI’s values—they are part of what the company believes is the right thing to do.

Application

Best Talent is managing the recruitment process and will treat all applications with strict confidentiality.

Please send your application in English, marked “1920/Associated Project Director, COWI”, to job@besttalent.dk. Interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible due to the urgency of this position. For more information about Best Talent, please visit www.besttalent.dk.

Are you passionate about combining deep product development expertise with compliance leadership to shape the next generation of water and climate solutions? Then join us in our mission to pioneer smarter solutions for moving and transforming water, reducing energy consumption, and enhancing quality of life for people.

As our new Compliance Engineer, you will be driving product design from concept to production readiness while building compliance expertise across the organization, interpreting international standards, and managing relationships with third-party agencies such as VDE and UL. You'll be part of a diverse, supportive and inclusive culture, that celebrates our differences and puts people first by fostering growth, well-being, and a sense of belonging.

What you will be doing

As a key part the Development team, you'll create impact by shaping how Grundfos develops compliant, world-class products by bridging the gap between engineering innovation and global regulatory requirements..

Your main responsibilities include:

•    Take ownership of defined product or technology areas, driving design, compliance and development from concept through production readiness

•    Proactively track new regulations and translate international standards into product-specific compliance requirements

•    Serve as the go-to person for global and regional compliance, managing Documents of Compliance and Technical Construction Files

•    Collaborate cross-functionally with manufacturing, quality, and supply chain teams to ensure successful product transfer across the value chain

•    Mentor fellow engineers, foster knowledge-sharing, and build compliance capabilities within the R&D function

•    Provide strategic input to the product development roadmap and drive compliance tasks within the task handling program

What makes you a great fit

Above all, you are a technically strong and collaborative engineer with deep product development experience, a keen eye for regulatory detail, and the ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders at a global level. We would also imagine that you have:

•    University degree or strong background in regulations, policy, compliance or risk management

•    Proven experience working with third-party certification agencies (e.g., VDE, UL, PFAS) and translating international standards into actionable product requirements

•    Solid knowledge of product development processes, lifecycle activities, and compliance/requirement management

•    Demonstrated ability to drive technical decisions and influence cross-functional stakeholders at a global level

It is a plus if you also:

•    Experience in large-scale manufacturing, preferably in pump technology or fluid handling

•    Track record of mentoring junior engineers and building team capabilities

•    Experience contributing to technology roadmaps and long-term product strategy

Why you will love working here

We care! Day to day, you can look forward to:

•    A working environment built around your needs, with flexible hours, home working opportunities and parental support.

•    Annual bonuses, health insurance and a strong focus on well-being activities.

•    Three days' additional paid leave for volunteering in your community.

•    Access to on-demand training and learning sessions and carefully structured programmes to pursue personal and professional development opportunities.

Are you ready to unlock possibilities at Grundfos? Apply today!

To get to know us better, follow us on LinkedIn or visit grundfos.com

About Grundfos

Grundfos is one of the world’s leading water technology companies with more than 19.000 employees in 60+ countries all over the world. Our skills commit us to pioneering solutions to the world’s water and climate challenges and improve the quality of life for people. We dare to do things that others cannot or dare not do, as we believe innovation is not only a business opportunity, but an obligation. And what really matters to us is not short term profit, but the impact we make. By becoming part of our united powerful team, you too can drive this change no matter your role.

An inclusive team

We believe that the key to a work environment, where employees thrive and grow, is our ability to celebrate and value our differences in background, experiences and perspectives. In our recruitment process we welcome all professional people without consideration of age, colour, gender identity, national origin, physical or mental disability, ethnicity or religion.

Next steps and how to apply

Ready to build, not just support?

Are you a curious and driven student who loves structure, details and making things work better? Do you want real responsibility, broad HR exposure, and the chance to help build HR processes in a global industrial company with more than 125 years of history?

At DISA Industries, part of the Norican Group, we are looking for a Student Assistant in HR who is ready to take ownership, ask questions, and help us strengthen and develop our HR foundation.

This is not a “fetch‑and‑file” student job. This is a role where you’ll learn, contribute, and grow.

Why You’ll Love Working with Us

• A small, dynamic HR setup – locally it will be you and the HR Business Partner, working closely together with real responsibility and short decision paths

• Hands‑on HR from day one – you’ll help build, structure and improve HR processes rather than just support existing ones

• Strong global backing – while the local team is small, we are part of a larger global HR team across the Norican Group

• A business in motion – DISA combines more than a century of industrial heritage with ongoing change, digitalisation and development

• A pragmatic, people‑focused environment where things get done through trust, collaboration and ownership

This role is ideal for you, if you thrive in a setting where you get responsibility, variety and ample of opportunities to learn. At DISA, many people stay for a long time – not because they have to, but because they want to.

Who You Are

You’re about to finish your bachelor’s degree or currently studying your master’s, for example cand.merc.psyk, cand.soc.hrm or a similar relevant programme, and you’re ready to put theory into practice.

You are:

• Proactive, driven and curious, with a strong sense of ownership

• Genuinely interested in HR processes, people data and organisational structures

• Structured, detail‑oriented and analytical. You like things to be correct and well‑organised

• Comfortable working independently and following tasks through from start to finish

• Motivated by learning and by being part of building something, not just maintaining it

Most importantly: you enjoy learning, improving things, are curious by heart and enjoy being part of a small dynamic team.

What We Offer

• A student job with substance, responsibility and learning

• Insight into HR in a global industrial organisation

• A chance to build skills that matter for your future career

• A welcoming, down‑to‑earth culture with high professionalism

This role is a strong match if you’re looking for a student job where you learn by doing, take responsibility, and build a solid foundation for a future HR career. You bring the curiosity and drive, and we will help develop your skillset.

What You’ll Do

Your tasks will evolve as you grow in the role, but will include a mix of operational HR work, such as:

• Supporting and developing core HR processes across the employee lifecycle

• Preparing and maintaining employment contracts, amendments and HR documentation for payroll

• Supporting the implementation and use of an HRIS, including data structure, quality and processes

• Ensuring HR data accuracy and well‑structured documentation

• Contributing to process design, standardisation and improvement

• Preparing analyses, overviews and HR material for local and global use

• Acting as a trusted HR support for employees and managers in daily matters

You’ll work closely with the HR Business Partner and gain insight into both local HR responsibility and global HR ways of working within Norican.

Want to know more? Ready to apply?

Ready to learn more and ready to apply?

We review applications continuously, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

If you want to build HR skills, take ownership, and be part of a company where people and values truly matter – we’d love to hear from you.

About Norican

NORICAN. Shaping Industry.

We are Norican, a global industrial group designing, building and supporting best‑in‑class machines and technologies for metal formation and surface treatment.

Bringing together five leading brands - DISA, Simpson, StrikoWestofen, Wheelabrator and Monitizer – we deliver one connected solution across the production process, supported by full‑service expertise and digital solutions.

Across green sand molding, die casting, sand preparation, melting, transport and dosing, and surface treatment, we help manufacturers improve performance and transform production across a wide range of industries. We build lifetime quality and long‑term partnerships by combining the strengths of our legacy brands to lead the industry through innovation, sustainability and profitable growth.

DISA

DISA design, build and support premium green sand moulding and cashing machines for the ferrous and non-ferrous foundry industries. For 125 years they have delivered machines that last for decades, and they are highly respected by customers and peers for excellent levels of quality and service. DISA machines keep customers producing relentlessly to the very highest standards. And they empower foundry productivity with a lifetime of efficient and a lower cost per casting.

Tembi is building the intelligence layer for European e-commerce.

We monitor more than 1 million online retailers across Europe and transform billions of datapoints into market intelligence that helps logistics providers, retailers and technology companies understand where the market is moving before their competitors do.

The next generation of market intelligence will not be built on static reports and dashboards. It will be built on continuously evolving data pipelines, AI-assisted enrichment, and systems capable of turning fragmented web signals into trusted commercial insight at scale.

We are at a rare moment in the company’s journey:

the market opportunity is large, our product is gaining traction across Europe, and the engineering team is still small enough that great engineers leave fingerprints on everything they build.

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer with strong foundations in Python, infrastructure, data engineering and large-scale data systems to help us build the core of that platform.

The team you’ll join

You will join a tight-knit engineering team of software engineers and data engineers working closely together to evolve our Market Intelligence platform.

We are around 20 colleagues today, with customers across Europe and a multicultural office in central Copenhagen.

We work with flat hierarchies, short decision paths and high ownership. Engineers at Tembi work closely with Product, Customer Success and customers themselves to understand real problems and ship solutions that create value quickly.

This is not an environment where engineers disappear into narrow silos or spend months building in isolation. We value pragmatic execution, strong collaboration and people who enjoy solving difficult problems head-on.

Current technology environment

Our platform and data infrastructure currently includes technologies such as:

• 
Python

• 
Azure

• 
MySQL

• 
Databricks

• 
Distributed scraping infrastructure

• 
Large-scale data processing pipelines

• 
CI/CD automation

• 
TypeScript services and tooling

We continuously evolve our architecture as we expand into new markets, products and AI-driven capabilities.

What you’ll do

• 
Evolve and maintain our scraping engine while expanding into new European markets and adapting to an increasingly dynamic and competitive web landscape.

• 
Design, build and maintain scalable data pipelines and backend services powering Tembi’s market intelligence platform.

• 
Explore practical applications of generative AI and LLMs to improve data extraction, classification, normalisation and enrichment at scale.

• 
Safeguard data quality, reliability and lineage across our platform so customers can trust the intelligence we deliver.

• 
Improve CI/CD workflows, observability and engineering practices to help the team ship safely and frequently.

• 
Collaborate closely with data scientists, product engineers and commercial teams to turn experiments into production-ready systems.

• 
Help shape the architecture of our data platform as we expand into new markets and product areas.

• 
Mentor other engineers and contribute to a pragmatic, responsible and high-trust engineering culture.

• 
Take ownership from idea to production — understanding both the technical and customer side of the problems you solve.

What success looks like after 12 months

• 
Expanded and stabilised data collection in new European markets.

• 
Improved reliability and quality of core datasets used directly by customers and AI models.

• 
Helped productionise AI-assisted enrichment and classification capabilities.

• 
Contributed meaningful improvements to platform scalability, observability and operational efficiency.

• 
Raised engineering standards through strong collaboration, ownership and pragmatic technical leadership.

• 
Delivered systems and improvements that customers actively use and see value from.

What we’re looking for

• 
6+ years of professional software engineering experience.

• 
Strong Python skills and experience building production-grade systems.

• 
Experience designing and operating scalable backend services and data pipelines.

• 
Strong SQL and database fundamentals.

• 
Hands-on experience with CI/CD, testing, deployment workflows and operational ownership.

• 
Experience working with cloud platforms such as Azure, AWS or GCP.

• 
Comfortable reasoning about performance, scalability, reliability and infrastructure cost.

• 
Experience with web scraping or large-scale open web data extraction.

• 
A pragmatic, ownership-driven mindset — you care about solving real customer problems, not just closing tickets.

Nice to have

• 
Experience applying LLMs or generative AI techniques to extraction, classification or enrichment problems.

• 
Experience with Databricks, Spark or modern lakehouse architectures.

• 
Experience with TypeScript and backend development beyond Python.

• 
Experience building internal tooling or developer platforms.

Why you’ll enjoy it here

• 
You will work on genuinely difficult engineering and data problems with direct business impact.

• 
Your work will influence product decisions, customer outcomes and the future direction of the platform.

• 
You’ll join a senior, highly collaborative team that values ownership, honesty and pragmatic engineering.

• 
We move fast, but we care deeply about building reliable systems and long-term value.

• 
You’ll have direct visibility into how customers use what you build — often within weeks, not quarters.

• 
We care more about curiosity, responsibility and impact than prestige or corporate titles.

• 
Our office is located in central Copenhagen at Fiolstræde near Nørreport, with canteen, snacks, soda and coffee included.

Compensation and growth

We are a startup building for long-term impact, not a large corporation optimising for hierarchy and process.

This role is best suited for engineers motivated by ownership, meaningful technical challenges, customer impact and the opportunity to help shape a growing platform and engineering culture from the inside.

Compensation is tailored individually based on experience, responsibilities and team fit.

Application process

The process starts with an initial review and introductory conversation.

Selected candidates will continue through technical and team interviews, and we may include a practical technical assessment and personality assessment as part of the process.

We aim to move quickly while making thoughtful decisions for both the candidate and the team.

This is not a consultancy opportunity, and we respectfully ask not to be contacted regarding consultancy offers.

Tembi is a platform that helps companies use open data about markets and companies to focus their strategy and implement it in the daily routines. Many companies are now able to use their own data about their customers and sales processes etc. (business intelligence). But accessing and using the vast amounts of data from the world outside is much more difficult. Most companies don't have the competencies to do it. That makes it difficult for these companies to act optimally in a dynamic world with uncertain information. We help solving this problem. We collect and combine vast amounts of data from different sources and countries. We apply economic impact models and advanced analytics to solve business critical questions for our customers, such as which markets should they focus on, where is the next big client for us, what do we need to do to be competitive? Our dashboard based solution is easy to use and enables everyone from C-level to the floor to act more efficiently. Come work with us! 👋 We are currently around 20 people in the Tembi team, mostly working within Business Development & Sales and Product Development. But will be growing even more over the coming months. Our office is located in Fiolstræde, right in the heart of Copenhagen. We do a lot of social activities together, and always try to celebrate our success in some way. We have one monthly social activity, such as sports or escape room etc. And we also have summer parties, christmas parties and a friday bar with a different theme every month. When the circumstances require it, we can of course work remotely, but we generally like working together in the office - and we have a super nice lunch every day. Our company culture is based on four pillars. This is who we are: - Inspiring friends - Agile ignitors - Confident navigators - Curious enthusiasts

Read more about Tembi

About the Job

Are you passionate about optimizing data platforms and ensuring seamless performance? Join our dynamic team in Copenhagen and play a key role in managing mission-critical database environments. We are a collaborative, solution-oriented team that thrives on innovation and efficiency.

As part of our Data Platforms team, you will work closely with developers, DevOps engineers, and system administrators to ensure high availability, security, and performance across on-premise SQL Servers and Azure SQL Managed Instances. This is an on-site position in Copenhagen with minimal travel expectations.

Responsibilities

• 
Diagnose and resolve database-related issues, including performance bottlenecks and connectivity problems.

• 
Optimize database performance through query tuning, indexing, and configuration adjustments.

• 
Manage and maintain SQL Server (2019–2022) and Azure SQL Managed Instances for high availability and security.

• 
Collaborate with developers and DevOps teams to automate provisioning, deployments, and monitoring using CI/CD pipelines.

• 
Implement security policies, access controls, and compliance measures.

• 
Maintain comprehensive documentation for configurations and troubleshooting.

Your Profile

You are a proactive team player with strong analytical and problem-solving skills. You communicate clearly, work collaboratively, and bring a positive, solution-oriented mindset to every challenge.

Required competencies:

• 
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, IT, or equivalent experience.

• 
5+ years of experience as a Database Administrator with expertise in troubleshooting and performance tuning.

• 
Strong knowledge of Microsoft Azure PaaS services and SQL Server environments.

• 
Familiarity with DevOps practices, version control (Git), and CI/CD pipelines.

•

Job Description

ServiceNow is its own department, and you will join a team of incredibly dedicated, ambitious and great colleagues. Our team works closely together on projects across the Nordics, combining the right expertise and competencies to deliver the best solutions for our clients. While we thrive on cross-border collaboration, you will also have a strong local presence in our Copenhagen office, where we emphasize teamwork, community, and a shared commitment to excellence.

In this role, you will make an impact by:

• Providing strategic advisory for some of the largest ServiceNow clients in Denmark and the Nordics.

• Engaging proactively with clients, advising on solution and problem scoping across the organization to ensure alignment with business objectives.

• Designing comprehensive solutions, including technical design using design thinking methodologies to ensure alignment with ServiceNow’s Enterprise Service Management capabilities and best practices.

• Helping our clients in defining and optimizing Service Management processes to drive efficiency.

• Offering insights and guidance on application development, agile development, software development lifecycle and cloud applications.

• Leading the delivery of solutions and support teams in corrective measures.

• Work closely with Program Leadership to oversee and lead multiple workstreams of technical design- and delivery activities, create and maintain a network of potential clients, and be known as a trusted advisor and participate in consulting sales activities, including writing service proposals.

Qualifications

By joining our team as a Manager, you will become part of and contribute to our shared success. You will build and nurture positive working relationships with teams and clients to exceed expectations. Key responsibilities and tasks will involve:

You have the following skills and experience:

• A minimum of 5 years of experience working with ServiceNow or other digitalization platforms.

• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.

• Hands-on experience leading end-to-end transformation projects in areas such as IT, HR, Finance, Risk or core business operations.

• Experience with IT Project Management and have the ability to oversee complex implementations and drive successful outcomes.

• Demonstrated consulting experience or prior experience as a Platform Owner, showcasing your ability to advise and lead clients through transformation initiatives.

• Familiarity with process frameworks such as Lean, TBM, ITIL or other methodologies relevant to your area of expertise.

• A strong technical background with an advanced understanding of key technical principles and best practices.

• Experience or a solid understanding of application development and software lifecycle management.

• Knowledge of technologies using client-server model and understanding of data-modelling, SQL data structures and system integrations.

• You are fluent in written and spoken English, and you should ideally have a high proficiency in Danish or a willingness to learn the language.

• You must have the right to live and work in Denmark.

Are you an experienced project professional who excels at building structure, driving consistency, and elevating project execution?

To support our growth and expanding portfolio of projects, we are strengthening our focus on the Project Management Office (PMO). You’ll get a key role in developing, maintain, train, and educate on the processes, methodology, and tool chain used in project execution.

Your Role

As PMO Lead, you will report to the Head of Projects & Delivery. You will become responsible for all aspects of our best-practice project execution and will be deeply involved in improving and developing our methodologies.

The PMO standardizes project practices, supports project managers and project teams, and represents a highly operational function.

The PMO ensures alignment with business goals by supporting Business Management and provides oversight across the project portfolio. The PMO spans governance, methodology, reporting, process development, and process control. The PMO leads the development of methodologies used during the scale-up of the organization – and may potentially evolve into the competence center for Project Management.

Your tasks include:

• Governance & Standards: Define, maintain, and continuously improve PM methodologies, templates, and best practices, ensuring compliance with processes, quality standards, and stage-gate governance.

• Project Monitoring & Reporting: Monitor project performance across scope, schedule, budget, and risks, and consolidate insights into portfolio dashboards and KPIs for leadership decision-making.

• Resource & Capacity Support: Support resource allocation and forecasting with Team Leads and Project Managers, identify bottlenecks, and help optimize utilization across the project portfolio.

• Support & Enablement: Enable Project Managers through coaching, training, and hands-on support with documentation, planning, tools, and evaluation of new project opportunities.

• Risk, Issue & Change Management: Support structured identification and handling of risks, issues, and changes, including escalation processes and decision forums.

• PMO Development: Drive continuous improvement of PMO methodologies and capabilities to support faster, more scalable, and predictable project delivery aligned with business growth.

The PMO Lead role is highly central to harmonizing and further professionalizing our project execution capability. Running activities according to standards, ensuring quality in execution, and ensuring predictability and repeatability will be key elements of our success. This work will happen in close collaboration with the Engineering Excellence Manager. Furthermore, the PMO Lead will act as the deputy to the Head of Projects & Delivery when required.

Short- and Long-Term Success

In the first 6–12 months, success means:

• Establishing clear structure and ownership of PMO processes and methodologies

• Delivering consistent, high-quality reporting and portfolio visibility

• Building trust and strong collaboration with project managers and key stakeholders

Longer term, you’ll take ownership of maturing the PMO into a scalable capability that supports faster, more predictable project execution, while acting as a competence center for project management across the organization.

What You Bring

You’re an experienced project professional with a strong knowledge of project, program, and portfolio management methodologies, and governance frameworks. You have the ability to design, implement, and continuously improve processes, standards, and tools. You have a strategic and analytical mindset that makes it possible to align project execution with business objectives.

You likely:

• Have 3+ years of PMO or similar experience

• Have 5+ years of project management experience

• Preferably, have a technical background as an engineer or equivalent higher education

• Balance supportive guidance with governance and control responsibilities

• Have the experience to drive change and ensure adoption of new processes and ways of working

Who You Are

You’re not just defining processes - you ensure they are used, understood, and create value. You take ownership of execution and help teams succeed through clarity, structure, and support.

You bring:

• Strong organizational awareness and ability to manage cross-functional complexity

• Excellent stakeholder management, influencing, and communication skills

• Continuous improvement mindset focused on efficiency, quality, and predictable delivery

• Capability to coach and develop project managers and build organizational competence

• True leadership: you take ownership of the PMO function and act with integrity
